outputs.L1: An active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly for conveying a fluid is disclosed. The assembly comprises a rotor assembly and a bearing assembly configured to support the rotor assembly contactlessly. The bearing assembly comprises an even number of electromagnetic units arranged around a central structure. Each electromagnetic unit comprises a first salient pole formed from a magnetic material, a permanent magnet providing a first magnetic pole, and a coil arranged around the salient pole. The bearing assembly further comprises an inner yoke having inner-yoke portions connected to the first salient pole of each electromagnetic unit and separated from one another by structural spacers. The inner yoke provides a closed first magnetic flux path passing through the rotor assembly and applying a first attractive force. The bearing assembly further comprises a position-stabilizing portion oriented perpendicular to the first attractive force acting on the rotor assembly. The coils provide an electromagnetic flux between each first salient pole and the rotor assembly to apply an adaptable axial force and/or tilting torque to the rotor assembly.
outputs.L2: An active magnetic rotor-bearing system for transporting fluid is described. The system includes a rotor assembly and a bearing assembly that supports the rotor assembly without physical contact. The bearing assembly contains an even number of electromagnetic units positioned around a central structure. Each unit includes a first salient portion made of magnetic material, a permanent magnet that establishes a first magnetic pole, and a coil surrounding the salient portion. The bearing assembly also includes an inter-yoke having separate portions connected to the first salient portion of each electromagnetic unit and divided from one another by structural spacers. This arrangement creates a closed first magnetic-flux path through the rotor assembly, thereby producing a first attractive force. A position-stabilizing portion acts on the rotor assembly in a direction perpendicular to that force. In addition, the coils generate electromagnetic flux between each first salient portion and the rotor assembly to apply an adjustable axial force, a tilting torque, or both to the rotor assembly.
outputs.L3:
The disclosed active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly is configured to convey a fluid through the rotation of a rotor assembly. Rather than relying on conventional mechanical bearings, the rotor assembly is supported without physical contact by a magnetic bearing assembly, thereby reducing friction and mechanical wear.

The bearing assembly includes an even number of electromagnetic units distributed around a central structure. Each electromagnetic unit comprises a magnetic salient, a permanent magnet that establishes a first magnetic pole, and an electromagnetic coil positioned around the salient. The salients of adjacent electromagnetic units are connected by inter-yoke portions, while structural spacers separate the inter-yoke portions from one another.

This arrangement establishes a closed magnetic-flux path extending through the rotor assembly. The resulting magnetic field applies an attractive force to the rotor assembly and supports it in a contactless manner. In addition, the assembly includes a position-stabilizing portion oriented perpendicular to the relevant bearing or rotor axis. By selectively controlling the electrical current supplied to the coils, the bearing assembly generates adjustable electromagnetic flux. This controllable flux produces adaptable axial forces and tilting torques, allowing the position and angular orientation of the rotor assembly to be actively stabilized during operation.
outputs.L4:
An active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly is configured to convey a fluid while supporting its rotor without mechanical contact. The rotor may carry an impeller, pump element, or other fluid-conveying structure and is positioned within a stationary magnetic assembly. Because the rotor is magnetically suspended, friction, mechanical wear, and contamination associated with conventional contact bearings can be reduced.

The stationary assembly includes an even number of electromagnetic units arranged around the rotor. Each unit includes at least one permanent magnet, an excitation coil, and one or more salient magnetic poles facing a magnetic portion of the rotor across a working air gap. The units also include respective inner-yoke portions that are magnetically separated from one another. This separation limits undesired magnetic coupling between adjacent units and permits the magnetic flux and force produced by each unit, or by opposing pairs of units, to be controlled with greater precision.

The permanent magnets establish a closed bias-flux path through the yokes, salient poles, air gaps, and rotor. The resulting permanent-magnet flux produces attractive forces that provide the basic bearing load required to support and center the rotor. Since this bias force is generated without continuous coil excitation, the assembly can maintain a substantial supporting force with relatively low electrical power consumption.

Current supplied to the coils generates a controllable electromagnetic flux that is superimposed on the permanent-magnet bias flux. Depending on the magnitude and direction of the current, the coil-generated flux strengthens the magnetic attraction at selected poles and weakens it at others. Coordinated control of the opposing electromagnetic units therefore produces an adjustable net axial force on the rotor. Differential excitation of circumferentially spaced units also generates a tilting moment, allowing the angular orientation of the rotor to be corrected about axes transverse to the rotor axis.

Position stabilizers are provided in mutually perpendicular directions to detect or counteract displacement of the rotor in the corresponding radial directions. The stabilizers may cooperate with position sensors and a feedback controller that determines rotor displacement, axial position, and angular inclination. Based on the detected operating state, the controller regulates the coil currents to restore the rotor to a desired contactless operating position. The even-numbered arrangement facilitates balanced operation by allowing diametrically opposed units to act as controlled pairs.

During fluid-conveying operation, hydraulic loads, pressure changes, rotor imbalance, and external disturbances may create axial forces or tilting torques. The active magnetic system responds by modifying the electromagnetic flux while the permanent magnets continue to provide the underlying bearing force. In this manner, the assembly combines passive magnetic biasing with active force control to achieve stable suspension over a range of loads and operating conditions.

The resulting rotor-bearing assembly supports and controls the fluid-conveying rotor without mechanical contact. Its closed permanent-magnet flux path provides efficient attractive bearing force, while independently adjustable coil excitation supplies the axial-force and tilting-torque corrections needed for dynamic stabilization. This configuration enables low-wear, low-friction, and adaptable rotor control, making it suitable for pumps and other fluid-handling equipment in which cleanliness, reliability, efficiency, or long service life is important.
outputs.L5:
### An Active Magnetic Bearing

An active magnetic bearing is a device that supports a rotating shaft without physical contact. Electromagnets generate controlled forces that keep the shaft suspended in the correct position. Sensors continuously measure its movement, while an electronic control system adjusts the magnetic field in real time.

Because there is no direct contact between moving components, active magnetic bearings experience very little friction and wear. They can operate at high speeds, require minimal lubrication, and produce less vibration than conventional bearings. These advantages make them suitable for turbines, compressors, electric motors, and other high-performance machines.

However, an active magnetic bearing requires a reliable power supply and a sophisticated control system. Backup bearings are also commonly installed to protect the machine if power is lost. Despite their complexity and cost, active magnetic bearings can improve efficiency, durability, and precision in advanced industrial applications.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a single patent-style claim for an active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly used to convey fluid, including permanent magnets, electromagnetic coils, salient poles, an inner yoke, magnetic flux paths, and rotor stabilization.
counterfactuals.output: 1. **An active magnetic rotor-bearing assembly for conveying a fluid, comprising:** a stator; a rotor disposed within the stator and defining an internal passage configured to convey the fluid; an inner yoke coupled to the rotor and extending circumferentially about the internal passage; a plurality of permanent magnets arranged circumferentially about the rotor; a plurality of salient poles supported by the stator and spaced from the rotor by respective magnetic air gaps; a plurality of electromagnetic coils respectively associated with the salient poles; and a controller configured to selectively energize the electromagnetic coils, wherein the permanent magnets, the inner yoke, the salient poles, and the magnetic air gaps define a plurality of magnetic flux paths that provide bias magnetic flux between the rotor and the stator, and wherein energization of the electromagnetic coils selectively modifies magnetic flux in the plurality of magnetic flux paths to generate magnetic bearing forces that maintain the rotor in a contactless, stabilized position relative to the stator while the rotor conveys the fluid through the internal passage.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention describing a contactless magnetic bearing for a fluid-conveying rotor assembly, using formal patent language.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a fluid-conveying rotor assembly comprising a rotor defining at least one fluid passage and a magnetic bearing configured to support the rotor without mechanical contact. The magnetic bearing includes rotor-mounted and stationary magnetic elements arranged to generate magnetic forces that maintain radial and/or axial alignment of the rotor during operation. The rotor is thereby rotatable relative to a housing while conveying fluid through the assembly, without requiring lubricated bearing surfaces in contact with the process fluid. The contactless arrangement reduces friction, wear, heat generation, and contamination, and may include passive magnetic elements, actively controlled electromagnetic elements, or a combination thereof to stabilize the rotor under varying operating conditions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a magnetic rotor-bearing system with an even number of electromagnetic units arranged around a central structure, capable of applying adjustable axial forces and tilting torque.
counterfactuals.output: A magnetic rotor-bearing system is disclosed in which an even number of electromagnetic units are circumferentially distributed about a central rotor or support structure. Each electromagnetic unit generates a controllable axial magnetic force across an associated air gap. Coordinated excitation of the units produces a resultant axial force for positioning or supporting the rotor, while differential excitation of diametrically opposed units generates a controllable tilting torque about one or more transverse axes. A controller independently adjusts the current supplied to the electromagnetic units in response to position, orientation, or load signals, thereby regulating axial displacement and angular alignment. The symmetric arrangement enables noncontact support, multidirectional tilt control, load balancing, and reduced mechanical wear in high-speed or precision rotating machinery.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

a magnetic support assembly arranged about the rotor and configured to maintain a clearance between the rotor and the magnetic support assembly, the magnetic support assembly comprising:

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a patented active magnetic bearing assembly in one paragraph, emphasizing its closed magnetic flux path, structure spacers, perpendicular stabilizing force, and adaptable electromagnetic control of the rotor.
counterfactuals.output: The patented active magnetic bearing assembly supports a rotor without mechanical contact by arranging ferromagnetic stator sections, rotor-facing poles, and magnetic structure spacers to form a substantially closed magnetic flux path with low leakage. The spacers maintain precise geometry and magnetic separation between structural components, while electromagnets selectively vary flux in the closed circuit to produce stabilizing forces perpendicular to the rotor’s axis or direction of motion. Position sensors and an adaptable feedback controller continuously adjust coil currents in response to rotor displacement, speed, or load, enabling dynamic centering, vibration suppression, and stable rotor control across changing operating conditions.
